messages:
maya: FYI folks — some new reports that the latest SDK release (v3.2.0) broke our example Vite + SWR sample app when used in edge runtimes. error is `Cannot find module` during client build.

sam: ugh, is this the conditional exports change we landed yesterday? saw some subtle differences in how bundlers resolve the `exports` map.

nora: Confirmed. The package `exports` now has only conditional `import`/`require` targets and no fallback for bundlers that expect a `default` entry. Vite's esbuild resolver ends up trying to load `./dist/index.cjs` and fails in the edge adapter.

maya: Repro steps I used: `pnpm install --filter examples/vite-swr && pnpm build` then `vercel dev` on edge adapter. Error snippet: ```Error: Cannot find module '/workspace/node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/index.cjs'```

tyler: Can you paste the `package.json` exports section?

maya: Sure: ```"exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }```

nora: Problem is a) some bundlers (and older node versions used by edge adapters) still need an unconditioned `.` entry that points to an interoperable build, and b) our `types` path is missing in the conditional map so TS inference in samples breaks too.

sam: Also noticed auth retry helpers were default-exported from `index.ts` before. With the ESM build the named/default interop changed and a tiny portion of sample apps that did `import sdk from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` now get `undefined` for `sdk.client`. That then triggers weird auth errors at runtime.

maya: Short-term mitigation: pin sample apps to the previous SDK version in package.json, and add a small README note. Medium-term: we should update our `exports` to include a neutral fallback and add `types`: ```"exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs", "default": "./dist/index.cjs" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }```

tyler: Adding a `default` key isn't standard in exports - some bundlers ignore it. I'd instead suggest adding a top-level `main` + `module` fields alongside `exports` so older tooling still finds something: ```"main": "dist/index.cjs", "module": "dist/index.mjs"``` and make sure `types` is present.

nora: +1 on `types` — we should also run our sample apps through a CI job that uses Vite + esbuild + vercel/edge runtime to catch regressions. Maybe a small smoke test that builds the example and runs a simple request.

sam: Another suggestion: for the short-term release toggle, we could publish a `compat` tag that includes the fallback `main/module/types` to give customers time to upgrade bundlers.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: pushed v3.2.1-compat -> registry.tgz (temporary compat build) :package: 

maya: Amazing, thanks CI. Will update the examples and open a PR for the CI smoke tests. Also documenting the breaking notes in the changelog so SDK integrators aren't surprised.

nora: I'll open a follow-up RFC to standardize our build outputs and ensure default export interop tests exist in the release checklist.

tyler: For tracking: create a short issue called "SDK exports: add bundler compat + types + CI smoke for examples" and link to this thread.

maya: Will do. Thanks all :sparkles:
